subject: Aligning PoC deployment constraints and trial success metrics

Subject: Aligning PoC deployment constraints and trial success metrics

Hi Cara — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the PoC mode (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private) and success criteria. I captured constraints you raised and a short timeline we can run in parallel with your security review.

Key constraints you mentioned
- PHI concerns for call transcripts and some PII in notes; primary requirement is no persistent customer data in shared model training.
- Audit and key management: on-prem KMS or customer-managed cloud KMS is preferred.
- Latency and throughput: target 95–99 pctl latency under 400ms for user-facing summarization; peak expected concurrent users ~150, steady-state 40–60 rps.
- Regional/data residency: US-only (east coast preferred).
- Procurement: finance needs an expected TCO for a 3-month PoC to evaluate operational costs.

Recommended PoC approach (what we usually see works)
- 2-week readiness + 3-week execution (5 weeks total):
  - Week 0–2: access & security onboarding (private endpoints/allowed IPs, KMS config, SOC2 evidence exchange)
  - Week 3–4: workload injection and performance tuning (batching, quantization profile)
  - Week 5: evaluation window and handoff (quality/regression checks, cost report)

Mode recommendation (based on constraints)
- Private VPC (customer-controlled) is our preferred path for PHI workloads if you want to avoid shared-hosting risk and bring-your-own-KMS. It supports your KMS/SEV controls and audit needs.
- If procurement/ops wants a quicker start, Dedicated capacity with reserved GPU pools in a US region is an alternative; it gives predictable throughput and we can surface audit logs and KMS integrations but involves hosting within Redwood infrastructure.
- Hosted API is fastest to start but requires strong contract-level controls and ingestion filters; we suggest Hosted only if you can accept non-customer-managed KMS and a short retention policy during the PoC.

Success criteria proposal (draft — please adjust)
- Functional: summaries match your rubric on 80%+ of sampled transcripts (we'll use your annotated 200-sample test set).
- Performance: 95th percentile latency < 350ms, sustained 50 rps with tail latency < 500ms.
- Cost: projected token cost < $1.80 per 1k tokens for the evaluation profile (we'll provide final numbers after model selection).
- Security/compliance: KMS integration validated, SOC2 evidence exchanged, and IP allowlist in place before workload run.

Immediate asks for HealthSync
1) Confirm preferred PoC mode: private-vpc OR dedicated-reserved OR hosted-api (one choice please).
2) Share: a) a redacted 200-sample test set (S3 link or Drive), b) an inventory of required integrations (KMS provider, SIEM), c) a contact for procurement.
3) Any hard blackout dates in Oct–Nov for your infra team?

I attached a one-pager PoC charter and a security checklist (stub). If this looks good, Marissa and I can schedule a 30-min kickoff with your infra and procurement next week.

Thanks —
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

- We are mandated to keep PHI in a customer-controlled environment. That pushes us toward private-vpc unless costs or procurement timelines make that infeasible.
- For KMS: we use AWS KMS with a customer-managed CMK in our account.
- Procurement: we need a 3-month cost estimate and a standard MSA addendum for limited data processing — finance will require that ahead of any reserved capacity commitment.
- Timeline: our infra team is available for onboarding the week of Oct 19 but not the week of Oct 12 (major platform maintenance).

Next steps from HealthSync
- I'll route a redacted 200-sample set via S3 by EOD Thu (we'll provide a temporary read-only link).
- Procurement contact: Priya Mehta (priya.mehta@healthsync.com). She will need the TCO and an outline of the security boundary.

If Private VPC is recommended, can you outline what we need to prepare on our side for network peering and egress monitoring? Also—what's the expected lead time to provision a Private control plane instance?

Great — thanks for confirming the PHI/KMS constraint, Cara. Short answers to your infra questions and a revised PoC timeline given your maintenance blackout: 

Private VPC prep (what we'll need from HealthSync)- VPC peering or Private Link config (we can take either; PrivateLink reduces routing complexity)- A dedicated subnet + NAT/egress path defined for outbound model fetches (if you allow egress)- AWS IAM role for Redwood service to access the S3 test set and to validate KMS key usage (we'll provide a minimal trust policy)- IP allowlist for the control plane management interface (we'll provide expected IP ranges)

Lead times and provisioning- Private control plane provisioning: typically 3–5 business days once networking and IAM info are provided. We can do parallel onboarding prep during your maintenance window and begin the performance phase the week of Oct 26.

Revised PoC schedule (based on your availability)- Oct 19–23: security & infra onboarding (Marissa leads)- Oct 26–Nov 08: performance tuning and workload run (2 weeks)- Nov 09–13: evaluation and final report (1 week)

Deliverables we will provide for procurement- 3-month projected TCO (line items: infra, model inference cost, engineer support)- MSA addendum template and a redlined example showing data processing limits

I'll attach a brief network checklist and an example minimal IAM role. Marissa — looping you to coordinate the Oct 19 kickoff and to share the checklist with HealthSync infra.

Logan
